config.title: Container orchestration

intro.title: Container orchestration
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn the fundamentals of container orchestration by setting up a simple multi-container application. You will explore core concepts like service discovery, load balancing, and automated deployment using a popular orchestration tool. The main technologies involved include Docker containers and a basic orchestration platform to manage them. By the end, you'll understand how orchestration helps scale and maintain applications efficiently in production environments.
intro.usecase: Container orchestration is the foundational pattern for managing and scaling modern cloud-native applications. It powers the deployment and operation of services in platforms like Kubernetes dashboards, where developers define and monitor pods, services, and deployments. This is critical for ensuring high availability in products like e-commerce sites during traffic surges or for rolling out updates seamlessly in SaaS applications without downtime.

objectives: Configure a basic container orchestration environment
Implement container deployment and scaling commands
Construct a service definition for container networking
Apply health check configurations to containerized applications
Manipulate container resource allocation and limits
Integrate persistent storage with container workloads
Control container lifecycle through orchestration commands

steps.title: Create main container orchestration demonstration component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ContainerOrchestrationDemo that will serve as the main demonstration component. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function ContainerOrchestrationDemo() { return null; } or const ContainerOrchestrationDemo = () => { return null; }.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly ContainerOrchestrationDemo and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the correct name and returned null.

steps.title: Initialize state for container cluster data
steps.instruction: Inside your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, initialize state using useState to hold container cluster information. Create a state variable named 'clusterData' with an initial value of an empty object {}.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to declare a state variable. The initial state should be an empty object that will later hold cluster data like nodes, pods, and services.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state for data
const [data, setData] = useState({});
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'clusterData' initialized as an empty object, ready to store container orchestration cluster information.
successCriteria: The useState hook is used to create a state variable named 'clusterData' with an initial value of {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useState correctly and naming the state variable 'clusterData' with an initial empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state. You need to use useState to create a state variable named 'clusterData' that starts as an empty object {}.

steps.title: Create the main orchestration dashboard structure
steps.instruction: In your ContainerOrchestrationDemo component, return a main dashboard container with three sections: one for cluster overview, one for node status, and one for container management.
steps.hint: Create a wrapper element (like a div) with three child elements that will serve as placeholders for each section.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic dashboard structure with three distinct sections for container orchestration monitoring.
successCriteria: The component returns a wrapper element containing three section elements representing cluster overview, node status, and container management areas.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three section elements inside your main wrapper for cluster overview, node status, and container management.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dashboard structure isn't quite right. You need to return a main wrapper element with three distinct section elements for the different monitoring areas.

steps.title: Add scaling controls and wire to scale handler
steps.instruction: Add a button to increase replicas and a button to decrease replicas inside your dashboard structure, and wire their onClick events to the scale handler function.
steps.hint: Create two button elements with appropriate labels like 'Increase Replicas' and 'Decrease Replicas', then set their onClick props to call your scale handler with the appropriate direction.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the dashboard UI that allow manual scaling of container replicas when clicked.
successCriteria: The dashboard contains an 'Increase Replicas' button and a 'Decrease Replicas' button, both wired to call the scale handler with appropriate parameters.

steps.instruction: Add a section with a button for automated workload balancing and a button for automated health monitoring, wiring each to their respective handlers.
